title: Measurement Backaction, Selective Reset, and Stability of M-Event Memory
content: Can a measurement cycle stabilize an observation response without erasing the event memory carried through it? We address this question in the classical variational event layer of a physical– observation dual-axis model. An explicit canonical record coupling preserves the selector angle but disturbs its conjugate charge, which also controls the subsequent response. We prove an obstruction to informative readout that preserves the complete selector pair on an open phase-space domain, and derive a resolution–backaction bound for smooth binary event cells. The free benchmark orbit is hyperbolic, with Floquet multipliers 2.408265755267 and 0.415236565073. A meridional reset  generated by a response potential and selective dissipation adds no selector phase. At fixed selector charge and with pair-transparent readout, its isotropic contraction factor stabilizes the response precisely when a < 0.415236565073. The attracting response circle retains a neutral phase direction; a convergent asymptotic-phase correction reduces the nearby dynamics to the original rotation. For independent Gaussian cycle noise, an exact Fourier law determines recurrence broadening. Unrestored  martingale charge kicks instead produce cubic accumulated phase variance in the linear response regime. The resulting theory separates response stabilization, instantaneous phase preservation, and conservation of the coupling that carries memory into the next event. It supplies calculable readout and reset mechanisms while preserving the original ideal M-event phase.
